preview: This episode looks at the connection between phones and attention. The problem is that staying focused may be harder when a phone is part of the situation. This matters because phones are part of many everyday tasks. By the end, you will understand what can make a phone difficult to ignore, even when you are trying to focus.
comment_1: Listen for how the study tested whether a familiar alert could affect attention.
comment_2: So far, we have seen that a phone alert can pull attention away from a task, even when you do not touch the phone. But what happens when the phone stays silent—does its location still matter?
comment_3: These studies show that a phone can affect our attention even when we are not using it. The change may begin with a sound, or with the phone simply being nearby. Next, we will look at two more ways to understand this finding.
comment_4: One point concerns attention when the phone is nearby, and the other concerns the habit of checking it. Let’s now bring these ideas together in the closing summary.
